```powershell
dotnet run --project src/web/MZikmund.Web --launch-profile https
```

Why the first line is mandatory: `$READER_TOKEN` and `$ADMIN_TOKEN` are minted against the **hosted** Supabase project, but in `Development` the `Supabase:LocalUrl` setting (`http://127.0.0.1:54321`) takes precedence, so the API would fetch JWKS from the **local** stack and reject both hosted tokens with `401` — including the admin one, which would make this gate unreadable. Emptying the variable makes this run validate against the hosted issuer. It is set for this shell only — close the shell, or run `Remove-Item Env:Supabase__LocalUrl`, once the gate has passed so ordinary local development gets the local stack back.

Expected: `Now listening on: https://localhost:7007`. Leave it running.

Terminal 2:

```bash
set -a; . "$SCRATCH/supabase.env"; set +a

echo -n "reader    -> "; curl -sk -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $READER_TOKEN" "https://localhost:7007/api/v1/admin/comments"
```

```
no token  -> 401
reader    -> 403
```

**STOP if any line differs.** Diagnosis:
- `reader -> 401` **and** `admin -> 401`: `Supabase__LocalUrl` was not cleared, so the API is checking hosted tokens against the local stack's JWKS and rejects both. Stop the app and start it again with `$env:Supabase__LocalUrl = ""` as in Terminal 1 above.
- `admin -> 401` alone: the token failed validation — re-mint it (Phase 1 Task 1.1 Step 6); a token older than its expiry, or a JWKS rotation inside the last ~10 minutes, both look like this.
- `admin -> 403`: `supabase:role` was not projected — decode `$ADMIN_TOKEN` and confirm `app_metadata.role = "admin"`.
- `reader -> 200`: the class-level `[Authorize(Policy = "AdminPolicy")]` is missing or the policy is not gating.
- `admin -> 404`: the `CommentsEnabledFilter` leaked onto this controller. It must **not** be here — moderation stays reachable while the feature is dark, which `Controller_IsNotGatedByTheCommentsEnabledFilter` asserts.

### Task 7.5: Refit Partial Interface and `MZikmundApiSerializerContext` Registrations

**Files:**
- Create: `src/shared/MZikmund.Api/IMZikmundApi.Comments.cs`
- Modify: `src/shared/MZikmund.Api/Serialization/MZikmundApiSerializerContext.cs` (using block; new `// Comment types` group before `// Common types`)
- Modify: `src/web/MZikmund.Web.Tests/MZikmund.Web.Tests.csproj` (add a `MZikmund.Api` project reference)
- Test: `src/web/MZikmund.Web.Tests/Serialization/MZikmundApiSerializerContextTests.cs`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: DTOs from `MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments`; the routes produced by Tasks 7.3 and 7.4.
- Produces: `MZikmund.Api.Client.IMZikmundApi` comment methods —
  `GetPostCommentsAsync`, `GetPostCommentsAuthenticatedAsync`, `GetCommentRepliesAsync`,
  `GetCommentRepliesAuthenticatedAsync`, `CreateCommentAsync`, `UpdateCommentAsync`,
  `DeleteCommentAsync`, `AddCommentVoteAsync`, `RemoveCommentVoteAsync`, `ReportCommentAsync`,
  `GetCommentReportsAsync`, `ResolveCommentReportAsync`, `GetModerationFeedAsync`,
  `CountNewCommentsAsync`, `HideCommentAsync`, `AdminDeleteCommentAsync`, `BanCommentAuthorAsync`.

> ### A SIGNED-IN CLIENT MUST CALL THE `...AuthenticatedAsync` READS
>
> `GetPostCommentsAuthenticatedAsync` and `GetCommentRepliesAuthenticatedAsync` are the **only** two
> methods that send an `Authorization` header on a read. The server fills `HasUpvoted` and `IsOwn`
> from the caller's identity, so a request without that header can only come back with
> `HasUpvoted = false` and `IsOwn = false` for **every** comment.
>
> Therefore: when `IUserService.IsLoggedIn` is true, call the `...AuthenticatedAsync` variant. Call
> the plain `GetPostCommentsAsync` / `GetCommentRepliesAsync` **only** when the user is signed out.
> Calling the plain variant while signed in is not a 401 and not a compile error — it silently
> renders an un-highlighted vote button and hides the author's own edit/delete affordances, which
> reads as a broken UI rather than as a bug in the call site. Phase 10 calls the Authenticated
> variants for exactly this reason.

> ### THESE METHOD NAMES ARE AUTHORITATIVE — LATER PHASES CALL THEM VERBATIM
>
> Step 7 below is the single declaration site. The four that drift most easily, with their exact
> signatures as declared there:
>
> ```csharp
> Task<ApiResponse<CommentDto>> AddCommentVoteAsync(Guid id);
> Task<ApiResponse<CommentDto>> RemoveCommentVoteAsync(Guid id);
> Task<ApiResponse<PagedResponse<CommentDto>>> GetModerationFeedAsync([Query] DateTime? since = null, [Query] int pageNumber = 1);
> Task<ApiResponse<int>> CountNewCommentsAsync([Query] DateTime? since = null);
> ```
>
> There is no `UpvoteCommentAsync`, no `RemoveCommentUpvoteAsync`, no `GetModerationCommentsAsync`
> and no `GetNewCommentsCountAsync`. A call site using those names does not compile — fix the call
> site, never rename this interface.

**Decision recorded here (this closes an open question in the research):** the two read endpoints get
**two** Refit methods each. The plain one carries no `[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]` so browsing a
post never triggers `AuthorizationHeaderValueGetter` and its interactive sign-in. The
`...AuthenticatedAsync` variant carries the header and is called by the app only when
`IUserService.IsLoggedIn` is true, which is what populates `HasUpvoted` and `IsOwn`.

```csharp
using MZikmund.DataContracts;
using MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments;
using Refit;

namespace MZikmund.Api.Client;

public partial interface IMZikmundApi
{
	// Reads come in two flavours on purpose. The plain method carries no Authorization header,
	// so browsing a post never triggers RefitSettings.AuthorizationHeaderValueGetter and its
	// interactive sign-in. The ...AuthenticatedAsync variant is called only when the user is
	// already signed in, and is what populates HasUpvoted / IsOwn.

	[Get("/v1/posts/{postId}/comments")]
	Task<ApiResponse<PagedResponse<CommentDto>>> GetPostCommentsAsync(
		Guid postId,
		[Query] CommentSortOrder sort = CommentSortOrder.Top,
		[Query] int pageNumber = 1);

	[Get("/v1/posts/{postId}/comments")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<PagedResponse<CommentDto>>> GetPostCommentsAuthenticatedAsync(
		Guid postId,
		[Query] CommentSortOrder sort = CommentSortOrder.Top,
		[Query] int pageNumber = 1);

	[Get("/v1/comments/{id}/replies")]
	Task<ApiResponse<PagedResponse<CommentDto>>> GetCommentRepliesAsync(
		Guid id,
		[Query] int pageNumber = 1);

	[Get("/v1/comments/{id}/replies")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<PagedResponse<CommentDto>>> GetCommentRepliesAuthenticatedAsync(
		Guid id,
		[Query] int pageNumber = 1);

	[Post("/v1/posts/{postId}/comments")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<CommentDto>> CreateCommentAsync(Guid postId, [Body] CreateCommentRequest request);

	[Patch("/v1/comments/{id}")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<CommentDto>> UpdateCommentAsync(Guid id, [Body] UpdateCommentRequest request);

	[Delete("/v1/comments/{id}")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<object?>> DeleteCommentAsync(Guid id);

	[Put("/v1/comments/{id}/vote")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<CommentDto>> AddCommentVoteAsync(Guid id);

	[Delete("/v1/comments/{id}/vote")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<CommentDto>> RemoveCommentVoteAsync(Guid id);

	[Post("/v1/comments/{id}/report")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<object?>> ReportCommentAsync(Guid id, [Body] ReportCommentRequest request);

	[Get("/v1/admin/comments/reports")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<PagedResponse<CommentReportDto>>> GetCommentReportsAsync([Query] int pageNumber = 1);

	[Post("/v1/admin/comments/reports/{commentId}/resolve")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<object?>> ResolveCommentReportAsync(Guid commentId);

	[Get("/v1/admin/comments")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<PagedResponse<CommentDto>>> GetModerationFeedAsync(
		[Query] DateTime? since = null,
		[Query] int pageNumber = 1);

	[Get("/v1/admin/comments/count")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<int>> CountNewCommentsAsync([Query] DateTime? since = null);

	[Post("/v1/admin/comments/{id}/hide")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<object?>> HideCommentAsync(Guid id);

	[Delete("/v1/admin/comments/{id}")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<object?>> AdminDeleteCommentAsync(Guid id);

	[Post("/v1/admin/authors/{id}/ban")]
	[Headers("Authorization: Bearer")]
	Task<ApiResponse<object?>> BanCommentAuthorAsync(Guid id);
}
```

## Phase 8: Migrate the web asset pipeline to esbuild

Phase 8 changes **how** the site's JavaScript is built and loaded. It adds **no** comments UI and **no** C# whatsoever. The acceptance bar is behavioural parity: the site must render and behave identically before and after, including the no-flash-of-wrong-theme guarantee.

Everything below was validated against a real copy of `Scripts/` in a scratchpad probe: `tsc 5.9.3 --noEmit` exits 0 over the converted tree, and `esbuild 0.28.2` emits `theme-init.js` 3.5 kb (IIFE), `site.js` 13.5 kb (flat ESM), `comments.js` 41 b.

Deliberate deviations from the researched proposal, stated up front:

1. A third file, `Scripts/check-bundles.mjs`, is added and wired as `npm run check:js` at the end of `npm run build`. It is the executable test for this phase — there is nothing else to unit-test in a bundler migration.
2. `Scripts/comments.ts` ships in this phase as a deliberately empty entry point exporting one no-op. The three entry points are a contract item; the UI that fills this one arrives later. An entry point that emits a zero-byte file would trip the wwwroot publish glob and `check:js`, hence the no-op rather than nothing.
3. `check:js` also asserts `site.js` has no top-level `export`. This is not in the research: `src/app/MZikmund.App/Templates/PostPreviewTemplate.html` line 11 loads `https://mzikmund.dev/js/site.js` as a **classic** script. Verified: with the repo's current `package.json` (no `"type"` field) esbuild emits flat ESM with zero exports, so that template keeps working — but adding `"type": "commonjs"` to `package.json` makes esbuild emit `export default B();` and silently breaks it. The check pins that down.

```json
{
	"compilerOptions": {
		"target": "ES2020",
		"module": "ESNext",
		"moduleResolution": "bundler",
		"lib": [ "ES2020", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable" ],
		"strict": true,
		"noImplicitAny": true,
		"noEmit": true,
		"isolatedModules": true,
		"verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
		"skipLibCheck": true,
		"forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
		"useDefineForClassFields": true,
		"allowJs": false,
		"types": []
	},
	"include": [ "Scripts/**/*.ts" ],
	"exclude": [ "node_modules", "wwwroot" ]
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the throwaway conversion script into the scratchpad**

The edit is mechanical and identical for all six files: delete the `namespace X {` line, delete the matching final `}`, dedent the body one level. `ReadingProgressBar.ts` uses 4 spaces, the other five use tabs — the script handles both and preserves CRLF. Write this to `C:\Users\Martin\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--Personal-mzikmund\876f8c04-94e6-4eda-91de-cdf93d49d494\scratchpad\convert-namespaces.mjs`:

```javascript
// One-shot, throwaway: turns `namespace X { export class Y }` files into plain
// ES modules by deleting the namespace wrapper and dedenting the body one level.
// Handles both tab-indented and 4-space-indented files. Keeps CRLF endings.

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

for (const file of process.argv.slice(2)) {
	const lines = readFileSync(file, 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').split('\n');

	const start = lines.findIndex(line => /^namespace\s/.test(line));
	if (start < 0) {
		throw new Error(`${file}: no top-level namespace found`);
	}

	let end = lines.length - 1;
	while (lines[end].trim() === '') {
		end--;
	}
	if (lines[end] !== '}') {
		throw new Error(`${file}: last non-blank line is not the namespace's closing brace`);
	}

	const body = lines.slice(start + 1, end).map(line =>
		line.startsWith('\t') ? line.slice(1) : line.startsWith('    ') ? line.slice(4) : line);

	const text = [...lines.slice(0, start), ...body]
		.join('\n')
		.replace(/^\n+/, '')
		.replace(/\s+$/, '') + '\n';

	writeFileSync(file, text.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n'), 'utf8');
	console.log(`converted ${file}`);
}
```

`Scripts/HeadingLinks.ts` must now read EXACTLY (this is the whole file — every other converted file follows the identical shape, class bodies unchanged):

```typescript
/**
 * Adds a copy-link button to each article heading.
 *
 * Depends on TableOfContents having run first — headings without an id are
 * skipped, and the TOC is what assigns them.
 */
export class HeadingLinks {
	private contentContainer: HTMLElement | null = null;

	public init(): void {
		if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
			document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => this.initialize());
		} else {
			this.initialize();
		}
	}

	private initialize(): void {
		this.contentContainer = document.querySelector('.post-content');
		if (!this.contentContainer) return;

		const headings = this.contentContainer.querySelectorAll('h2, h3, h4');
		headings.forEach((heading) => {
			const el = heading as HTMLElement;
			if (!el.id) return;

			const button = document.createElement('button');
			button.type = 'button';
			button.className = 'heading-copy-link';
			button.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Copy link to this section');
			button.title = 'Copy link';
			// Uses the shared inline sprite rather than a bespoke inline SVG.
			button.innerHTML = '<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-link-45deg"></use></svg>';

			button.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
				e.preventDefault();
				e.stopPropagation();
				const url = `${window.location.origin}${window.location.pathname}#${el.id}`;
				// clipboard.writeText needs a secure context and can reject —
				// handle rejection rather than leaving it unhandled.
				navigator.clipboard?.writeText(url).then(
					() => this.showCopiedFeedback(button),
					() => { /* copying unavailable; nothing useful to show */ }
				);
			});

			el.appendChild(button);
		});
	}

	private showCopiedFeedback(button: HTMLElement): void {
		button.classList.add('is-copied');
		setTimeout(() => button.classList.remove('is-copied'), 1500);
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Split `ThemeSwitchManager.init()` in two**

This is the one non-mechanical change: `theme-init.js` must apply the theme render-blocking, while `site.js` (a deferred module) only wires up the flyout. In `src/web/MZikmund.Web/Scripts/ThemeSwitchManager.ts` replace:

```typescript
	public static init(): void {
		// Runs render-blocking in <head> so the theme is applied before the
		// first paint — without this there is a flash of the wrong theme.
		ThemeSwitchManager.applyTheme(ThemeSwitchManager.readPreference());

		document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => ThemeSwitchManager.wireUp());
	}
```

with:

```typescript
	/** Entry point of theme-init.js: blocking in <head>, before first paint. */
	public static applyStoredTheme(): void {
		ThemeSwitchManager.applyTheme(ThemeSwitchManager.readPreference());
	}

	/**
	 * Called from site.ts, which is a deferred module script. The readyState
	 * guard matches the pattern the other modules already use and keeps this
	 * correct if the tag ever loses type="module".
	 */
	public static init(): void {
		if (document.readyState === "loading") {
			document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => ThemeSwitchManager.wireUp());
		} else {
			ThemeSwitchManager.wireUp();
		}
	}
```

This is `index.ts` with the six `/// <reference>` comments replaced by real imports. The initialisation ORDER and its comments are preserved verbatim — `TableOfContents` assigns ids to headings that lack them and `HeadingLinks` skips any heading without one, so swapping those two silently kills every heading anchor.

```typescript
// Bundled to wwwroot/js/site.js as an ES module. Module scripts are deferred by
// default, which is what every module below already assumes.
import { ThemeSwitchManager } from "./ThemeSwitchManager";
import { SiteNav, BackToTop, ContentEnhancements } from "./SiteNav";
import { ConnectedAnimation, Reveal } from "./Motion";
import { ReadingProgressBar } from "./ReadingProgressBar";
import { TableOfContents } from "./TableOfContents";
import { HeadingLinks } from "./HeadingLinks";

// Wires up the theme flyout. The theme itself was already applied by
// theme-init.js, render-blocking, before first paint.
ThemeSwitchManager.init();

new SiteNav().init();
new BackToTop().init();
new ContentEnhancements().init();

// Fluent motion: connected animation between a card and its post, and the
// pointer-tracked Reveal highlight. Both are no-ops without support or when
// the visitor prefers reduced motion.
new ConnectedAnimation().init();
new Reveal().init();

new ReadingProgressBar().init();

// Order matters: TableOfContents assigns ids to headings that lack them, and
// HeadingLinks skips any heading without one.
new TableOfContents().init();
new HeadingLinks().init();
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `esbuild@0.28.2` from Task 8.1; `Scripts/theme-init.ts`, `Scripts/site.ts`, `Scripts/comments.ts` from Task 8.2.
- Produces: `wwwroot/js/theme-init.js` (IIFE, classic), `wwwroot/js/site.js` (ESM, no top-level exports), `wwwroot/js/comments.js` (ESM). npm scripts `typecheck`, `build:js`, `check:js`, `watch:js`; `build:ts` and `watch:ts` are gone.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the test first — `src/web/MZikmund.Web/Scripts/check-bundles.mjs`**

```javascript
// Guards the three bundles esbuild is supposed to produce.
//
// theme-init.js must stay a classic IIFE: a module script is ALWAYS deferred,
// and a deferred theme applier means every dark-mode visitor gets a flash of
// white before first paint.
//
// site.js must stay free of top-level import/export too, because the Uno app's
// Templates/PostPreviewTemplate.html loads it as a plain <script> — a stray
// `export` there is a SyntaxError that kills the whole file. Adding
// "type": "commonjs" to package.json is what makes esbuild emit one.

import { readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const OUT = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', 'wwwroot', 'js');

// Matches a real ESM statement, not the word "export" inside an identifier or a
// property access such as `module.exports`.
const TOP_LEVEL_ESM = /(?:^|[^.\w$])(?:import|export)\s*(?:default|[{*]|var |let |const |function |class )/;

const failures = [];

function read(name) {
	let size;
	try {
		size = statSync(join(OUT, name)).size;
	} catch {
		failures.push(`${name}: missing from wwwroot/js`);
		return null;
	}
	if (size === 0) {
		failures.push(`${name}: file is empty`);
		return null;
	}
	return readFileSync(join(OUT, name), 'utf8');
}

const themeInit = read('theme-init.js');
const site = read('site.js');
read('comments.js');

if (themeInit !== null) {
	if (TOP_LEVEL_ESM.test(themeInit)) {
		failures.push('theme-init.js: has a top-level import/export, so it is not a classic script');
	}
	if (!themeInit.includes('data-theme')) {
		failures.push('theme-init.js: never writes data-theme, so the theme applier is not in the bundle');
	}
}

if (site !== null && TOP_LEVEL_ESM.test(site)) {
	failures.push('site.js: has a top-level import/export, which breaks PostPreviewTemplate.html');
}

if (failures.length > 0) {
	console.error('check:js FAILED');
	for (const failure of failures) {
		console.error(`  - ${failure}`);
	}
	process.exit(1);
}

console.log('check:js OK - theme-init.js (iife), site.js, comments.js');
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `src/web/MZikmund.Web/Scripts/build-js.mjs`**

```javascript
// Bundles Scripts/*.ts into wwwroot/js with esbuild.
//
//   theme-init.js  IIFE, render-blocking classic <script> in <head>
//   site.js        ESM, <script type="module">, every page
//   comments.js    ESM, <script type="module">, post pages only
//
// Two passes because the formats differ: a module script is ALWAYS deferred, so
// the theme applier — which must run before first paint — cannot be one.
//
// esbuild does NOT type-check. `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit) is the gate,
// and it runs before this script in `npm run build`.
//
// Filenames are fixed and unhashed on purpose: asp-append-version="true" already
// cache-busts via query string, and MSBuild globs wwwroot at evaluation time (see
// the note in .gitignore), so a name that changes between builds would go missing
// from the publish output. Do not enable `splitting` — it emits hashed chunks.

import { build, context } from 'esbuild';
import { rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const ROOT = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const OUT = join(ROOT, 'wwwroot', 'js');
const prod = process.argv.includes('--prod');
const watch = process.argv.includes('--watch');

// esbuild never removes stale output, and wwwroot/js holds nothing but generated
// files (it is gitignored in full), so wipe it rather than leak renamed entries
// into the publish glob.
rmSync(OUT, { recursive: true, force: true });

const shared = {
	absWorkingDir: ROOT,
	bundle: true,
	target: ['es2020'],
	charset: 'utf8',
	legalComments: 'none',
	minify: prod,
	sourcemap: prod ? false : 'linked',
	logLevel: 'info',
};

const configs = [
	{
		...shared,
		entryPoints: [join(ROOT, 'Scripts', 'theme-init.ts')],
		outfile: join(OUT, 'theme-init.js'),
		format: 'iife',
	},
	{
		...shared,
		entryPoints: [
			join(ROOT, 'Scripts', 'site.ts'),
			join(ROOT, 'Scripts', 'comments.ts'),
		],
		outdir: OUT,
		format: 'esm',
		splitting: false,
	},
];

if (watch) {
	for (const config of configs) {
		const ctx = await context(config);
		await ctx.watch();
	}
	console.log('esbuild: watching Scripts/**');
} else {
	await Promise.all(configs.map(build));
}
```

Do NOT collapse this workflow's `dotnet build` + `dotnet publish` into a single publish. - [ ] **Step 2: Document the asset pipeline in `docs/design-system.md`**

Insert a new section immediately before the `## Contract with JavaScript` heading. Replace:

```markdown

## Contract with JavaScript
```

with:

```markdown
Prefer letting a component own its spacing over reaching for a utility.

## Asset pipeline

`npm run build` (run automatically by `dotnet build` via the `NpmBuild` MSBuild
target) does five things: generates fonts and the icon sprite, compiles SCSS to
`site.css` and `site.min.css`, type-checks with `tsc --noEmit`, bundles
TypeScript with esbuild, and verifies the bundles.

TypeScript is bundled by esbuild into three fixed, unhashed entry points:

| Output | Format | Loaded as | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wwwroot/js/theme-init.js` | IIFE | blocking classic `<script>` | every page, in `<head>` |
| `wwwroot/js/site.js` | ESM | `<script type="module">` | every page, in `<head>` |
| `wwwroot/js/comments.js` | ESM | `<script type="module">` | post pages only |

Three rules hold this together:

- `theme-init.js` must never become a module. Module scripts are ALWAYS
  deferred, and a deferred theme applier is a flash of the wrong theme on every
  navigation for every dark-mode visitor.
- `site.js` must never gain a top-level `export`. The Uno app's
  `Templates/PostPreviewTemplate.html` loads it as a plain `<script>`.
- Filenames stay fixed and unhashed. `asp-append-version="true"` already
  cache-busts via query string, and MSBuild globs `wwwroot` at evaluation time,
  so a name that changes between builds goes missing from the publish output.
  Do not enable esbuild's `splitting`.

`npm run check:js` (`Scripts/check-bundles.mjs`) enforces all three.
```

## Phase 9: Web comments UI — server-rendered partial, hydration, sign-in and write-then-auth

**Scope note (deliberate, state it rather than discover it):** the web app registers only `AddJwtBearer` — Razor Pages always see an anonymous `HttpContext.User`. So the server-rendered comment list always carries `HasUpvoted = false` and `IsOwn = false`. The hydration module therefore re-fetches the current page with the bearer token when a session exists and replaces the list; anonymous readers keep the server markup untouched. For the same reason the no-JS state is **read-only**: the composer is rendered with the `hidden` attribute and only `comments.ts` reveals it.

**Also deliberate:** the `Top | Newest` toggle is a real link (`?sort=new#comments`) resolved server-side, not a JS interception — it keeps both orders readable and crawlable without JavaScript. Inline *editing* of a comment is intentionally not built on the web in v1; the `PATCH` endpoint is exercised by the Uno app. Delete-own and report are built here.

**Prerequisite phases assumed complete:** the esbuild bundler phase (`Scripts/build-js.mjs`, `Scripts/theme-init.ts`, `Scripts/site.ts`, the replaced `tsconfig.json`, `@supabase/supabase-js@2.112.3` + `esbuild@0.28.2` in `package.json`), the data/handler phase (`GetPostCommentsQuery`, `GetCommentRepliesQuery`, `CommentDto`), and the API phase (`CommentsController`, `CommentsOptions`, `SupabaseOptions`, `TurnstileOptions` registered in `Program.cs`).

### Task 9.2: `FindCommentPageQuery` — server-side deep-link page resolution

A URL fragment never reaches the server, so `/blog/{routeName}?comment={id}` must be resolved to a page number in the PageModel before the list is queried. Nothing in the contract provides this, so this task defines it.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/web/MZikmund.Web.Core/Features/Comments/CommentPaging.cs`
- Create: `src/web/MZikmund.Web.Core/Features/Comments/FindCommentPageQuery.cs`
- Create: `src/web/MZikmund.Web.Core/Features/Comments/FindCommentPageHandler.cs`
- Test: `src/web/MZikmund.Web.Core.Tests/Features/Comments/FindCommentPageHandlerTests.cs`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `MZikmund.Web.Data.DatabaseContext` with `DbSet<CommentEntity> Comment`; `MZikmund.Web.Data.Entities.CommentEntity`; `MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments.CommentSortOrder`; `MZikmund.Web.Data.Entities.CommentStatus`. Also consumes the `CommentsController` route table exactly as Phase 7 Task 7.3's attribute-route tests already assert it — `"posts/{postId}/comments"` and `"comments/{id}/replies"` with **no** `:guid` constraints, and a reply page size of **20**. Phase 7 WINS: Step 2 below only adds the defaulted `pageSize` parameters and changes nothing else about those two actions.
- Produces:
  - `public static class CommentPaging` in `MZikmund.Web.Core.Features.Comments` with `public const int DefaultPageSize = 20;` and `public const int DefaultReplyPageSize = 20;` — 20, not 10: Phase 7 Task 7.3 asserts `It.Is<GetCommentRepliesQuery>(q => q.CommentId == CommentId && q.PageSize == 20)`.
  - `public record FindCommentPageQuery(Guid CommentId, CommentSortOrder Sort, int PageSize) : IRequest<int?>;` — returns the 1-based page number of the top-level comment that contains `CommentId`, or `null` when the comment does not exist or is hidden by a moderator.

- [ ] **Step 1: Add the shared page-size constants**

Create `src/web/MZikmund.Web.Core/Features/Comments/CommentPaging.cs`:

```csharp
namespace MZikmund.Web.Core.Features.Comments;

/// <summary>
/// Page sizes shared by the API, the Razor page and the browser module, so the
/// server-rendered first page and the client's "Load more" cannot disagree.
/// </summary>
public static class CommentPaging
{
	/// <summary>Top-level comments per page.</summary>
	public const int DefaultPageSize = 20;

	/// <summary>
	/// Replies per page when the overflow is expanded. The same 20 as the
	/// top-level size, because the controller test asserts the reply query is
	/// sent with PageSize == 20.
	/// </summary>
	public const int DefaultReplyPageSize = 20;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Pin the controller and the API to the same page size**

Open `src/web/MZikmund.Web/Controllers/CommentsController.cs` and make the two `[AllowAnonymous]` GET actions take an explicit, defaulted `pageSize`, so the client can page consistently.

Change **nothing else** about those two actions' route templates, names or existing attributes — the
only edits are the added `pageSize` parameter, the typed 200 response, and the two using directives
below. The route templates stay byte-identical to the contract's route table — no `:guid` constraints — because Phase 7 Task 7.3 asserts them literally with
`[InlineData(nameof(CommentsController.GetPostComments), typeof(HttpGetAttribute), "posts/{postId}/comments")]` and
`[InlineData(nameof(CommentsController.GetCommentReplies), typeof(HttpGetAttribute), "comments/{id}/replies")]`,
and it verifies the reply call with `It.Is<GetCommentRepliesQuery>(q => q.CommentId == CommentId && q.PageSize == 20)`.
Adding a constraint, or lowering the reply page size to 10, turns three already-green Phase 7 tests red.

The signatures must read exactly:

```csharp
	[HttpGet("posts/{postId}/comments")]
	[AllowAnonymous]
	[ProducesResponseType(typeof(PagedResponse<CommentDto>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
	[ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
	public async Task<IActionResult> GetPostComments(
		Guid postId,
		[FromQuery] CommentSortOrder sort = CommentSortOrder.Top,
		[FromQuery] int pageNumber = 1,
		[FromQuery] int pageSize = CommentPaging.DefaultPageSize) =>
		Ok(await _mediator.Send(new GetPostCommentsQuery(postId, sort, pageNumber, pageSize)));

	[HttpGet("comments/{id}/replies")]
	[AllowAnonymous]
	[ProducesResponseType(typeof(PagedResponse<CommentDto>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
	[ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
	public async Task<IActionResult> GetCommentReplies(
		Guid id,
		[FromQuery] int pageNumber = 1,
		[FromQuery] int pageSize = CommentPaging.DefaultReplyPageSize) =>
		Ok(await _mediator.Send(new GetCommentRepliesQuery(id, pageNumber, pageSize)));
```

Note the `[ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]` line on each action: Phase 7 Task 7.1
already declared it, and the only change here is that the 200 response becomes *typed*. Do not drop it.

Two using directives are required for the block above to compile:

```csharp
using MZikmund.DataContracts;                  // PagedResponse<T>
using MZikmund.Web.Core.Features.Comments;     // CommentPaging, the queries
```

`using MZikmund.Web.Core.Features.Comments;` is already present from Phase 7.
**`using MZikmund.DataContracts;` is not** — `MZikmund.Web` has no `GlobalUsings.cs` and
`ImplicitUsings` does not cover it, so omitting it is `CS0246: The type or namespace name
'PagedResponse<>' could not be found`. Add it.

Finally, delete Phase 7's now-unreferenced `private const int PageSize = 20;` and
`private const int RepliesPageSize = 20;` from `CommentsController` — the defaults above come from
`CommentPaging`, so leaving them is two dead constants and a second source of truth.

Create `src/web/MZikmund.Web.Core.Tests/Features/Comments/FindCommentPageHandlerTests.cs`:

```csharp
using System;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.Data.Sqlite;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions;
using MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments;
using MZikmund.Web.Core.Features.Comments;
using MZikmund.Web.Data;
using MZikmund.Web.Data.Entities;
using Xunit;

namespace MZikmund.Web.Core.Tests.Features.Comments;

public class FindCommentPageHandlerTests : IDisposable
{
	private static readonly Guid PostId = new("11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111");
	private static readonly Guid AuthorId = new("22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222");
	private static readonly DateTime Origin = new(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, DateTimeKind.Utc);

	private readonly SqliteConnection _connection;
	private readonly DatabaseContext _dbContext;

	public FindCommentPageHandlerTests()
	{
		_connection = new SqliteConnection("DataSource=:memory:");
		_connection.Open();

		DbContextOptions<DatabaseContext> options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<DatabaseContext>()
			.UseSqlite(_connection)
			.Options;

		_dbContext = new DatabaseContext(options);
		_dbContext.Database.EnsureCreated();

		_dbContext.Post.Add(new PostEntity { Id = PostId, RouteName = "post", Title = "Post" });
		_dbContext.CommentAuthor.Add(new CommentAuthorEntity
		{
			Id = AuthorId,
			DisplayName = "Reader",
			Email = "reader@example.com",
			CreatedOn = Origin,
			LastSeenOn = Origin,
		});
		_dbContext.SaveChanges();
	}

	public void Dispose()
	{
		_dbContext.Dispose();
		_connection.Dispose();
		GC.SuppressFinalize(this);
	}

	private FindCommentPageHandler CreateHandler() =>
		new(_dbContext, NullLogger<FindCommentPageHandler>.Instance);

	private CommentEntity AddComment(int minutesAfterOrigin, int upvotes, Guid? parentId = null)
	{
		CommentEntity comment = new()
		{
			Id = Guid.NewGuid(),
			PostId = PostId,
			ParentId = parentId,
			AuthorId = AuthorId,
			Content = "hello",
			ContentHtml = "<p>hello</p>",
			Status = CommentStatus.Visible,
			CreatedOn = Origin.AddMinutes(minutesAfterOrigin),
			UpvoteCount = upvotes,
		};

		_dbContext.Comment.Add(comment);
		_dbContext.SaveChanges();
		return comment;
	}

	[Fact]
	public async Task Handle_UnknownComment_ReturnsNull()
	{
		// Arrange
		FindCommentPageHandler handler = CreateHandler();
		FindCommentPageQuery query = new(Guid.NewGuid(), CommentSortOrder.New, 20);

		// Act
		int? page = await handler.Handle(query, CancellationToken.None);

		// Assert
		Assert.Null(page);
	}

	[Fact]
	public async Task Handle_NewSortTwentyFirstNewest_ReturnsTwo()
	{
		// Arrange
		CommentEntity target = null!;
		for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++)
		{
			CommentEntity created = AddComment(minutesAfterOrigin: i, upvotes: 0);
			if (i == 4)
			{
				// 24 comments are newer than this one, so it is the 25th in
				// newest-first order and lands on page 2 with a page size of 20.
				target = created;
			}
		}

		FindCommentPageHandler handler = CreateHandler();
		FindCommentPageQuery query = new(target.Id, CommentSortOrder.New, 20);

		// Act
		int? page = await handler.Handle(query, CancellationToken.None);

		// Assert
		Assert.Equal(2, page);
	}

	[Fact]
	public async Task Handle_ReplyOnSecondPage_ReturnsPageOfItsParent()
	{
		// Arrange
		CommentEntity parent = null!;
		for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++)
		{
			CommentEntity created = AddComment(minutesAfterOrigin: i, upvotes: 0);
			if (i == 0)
			{
				parent = created;
			}
		}

		CommentEntity reply = AddComment(minutesAfterOrigin: 100, upvotes: 0, parentId: parent.Id);

		FindCommentPageHandler handler = CreateHandler();
		FindCommentPageQuery query = new(reply.Id, CommentSortOrder.New, 20);

		// Act
		int? page = await handler.Handle(query, CancellationToken.None);

		// Assert
		Assert.Equal(2, page);
	}

	[Fact]
	public async Task Handle_TopSort_OrdersByUpvotesThenOldestFirst()
	{
		// Arrange
		AddComment(minutesAfterOrigin: 0, upvotes: 10);
		AddComment(minutesAfterOrigin: 1, upvotes: 10);
		CommentEntity target = AddComment(minutesAfterOrigin: 2, upvotes: 10);
		AddComment(minutesAfterOrigin: 3, upvotes: 99);

		FindCommentPageHandler handler = CreateHandler();
		// Page size 3: the 99-upvote comment plus the two older 10-upvote ones
		// fill page 1, so the target is the first entry of page 2.
		FindCommentPageQuery query = new(target.Id, CommentSortOrder.Top, 3);

		// Act
		int? page = await handler.Handle(query, CancellationToken.None);

		// Assert
		Assert.Equal(2, page);
	}

	[Fact]
	public async Task Handle_HiddenByModerator_ReturnsNull()
	{
		// Arrange
		CommentEntity hidden = AddComment(minutesAfterOrigin: 0, upvotes: 0);
		hidden.Status = CommentStatus.HiddenByModerator;

		// Act
		int? page = await handler.Handle(query, CancellationToken.None);

		// Assert
```

```csharp
using MediatR;
using MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments;

namespace MZikmund.Web.Core.Features.Comments;

/// <summary>
/// Resolves the 1-based page of top-level comments that contains
/// <paramref name="CommentId"/> (or its parent, when it is a reply).
/// Returns <c>null</c> when the comment does not exist or is hidden.
/// </summary>
public record FindCommentPageQuery(Guid CommentId, CommentSortOrder Sort, int PageSize) : IRequest<int?>;
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Add the handler**

Create `src/web/MZikmund.Web.Core/Features/Comments/FindCommentPageHandler.cs`:

```csharp
using MediatR;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments;
using MZikmund.Web.Data;
using MZikmund.Web.Data.Entities;

namespace MZikmund.Web.Core.Features.Comments;

internal sealed class FindCommentPageHandler : IRequestHandler<FindCommentPageQuery, int?>
{
	private readonly DatabaseContext _dbContext;
	private readonly ILogger<FindCommentPageHandler> _logger;

	public FindCommentPageHandler(
		DatabaseContext dbContext,
		ILogger<FindCommentPageHandler> logger)
	{
		_dbContext = dbContext;
		_logger = logger;
	}

	public async Task<int?> Handle(FindCommentPageQuery request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
	{
		var target = await _dbContext.Comment
			.AsNoTracking()
			.Where(c => c.Id == request.CommentId)
			.Select(c => new { c.Id, c.ParentId })
			.FirstOrDefaultAsync(cancellationToken);

		if (target is null)
		{
			_logger.LogInformation("Deep link to unknown comment {CommentId}.", request.CommentId);
			return null;
		}

		// Only top-level comments are paged; a reply lives on its parent's page.
		Guid anchorId = target.ParentId ?? target.Id;

		var anchor = await _dbContext.Comment
			.AsNoTracking()
			.Where(c => c.Id == anchorId)
			.Select(c => new { c.PostId, c.CreatedOn, c.UpvoteCount, c.Status })
			.FirstOrDefaultAsync(cancellationToken);

		if (anchor is null || anchor.Status == CommentStatus.HiddenByModerator)
		{
			return null;
		}

		// Must match the ordering and filtering of GetPostCommentsHandler:
		// moderator-hidden comments are excluded, author tombstones are kept.
		IQueryable<CommentEntity> siblings = _dbContext.Comment
			.AsNoTracking()
			.Where(c => c.PostId == anchor.PostId
				&& c.ParentId == null
				&& c.Status != CommentStatus.HiddenByModerator);

		int precedingCount = request.Sort == CommentSortOrder.New
			? await siblings.CountAsync(c => c.CreatedOn > anchor.CreatedOn, cancellationToken)
			: await siblings.CountAsync(
				c => c.UpvoteCount > anchor.UpvoteCount
					|| (c.UpvoteCount == anchor.UpvoteCount && c.CreatedOn < anchor.CreatedOn),
				cancellationToken);

		int pageSize = request.PageSize < 1 ? 1 : request.PageSize;
		return (precedingCount / pageSize) + 1;
	}
}
```

```csharp
using System.Text.Json;
using MZikmund.DataContracts;
using MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments;

namespace MZikmund.Web.Pages.Blog;

/// <summary>
/// Everything _Comments.cshtml needs. Deliberately its own model rather than a
/// widening of IPostPageModel, which is shared with the draft preview page.
/// </summary>
public class CommentsSectionModel
{
	/// <summary>Post the comments belong to.</summary>
	public required Guid PostId { get; init; }

	/// <summary>Top-level comments for the resolved page.</summary>
	public required PagedResponse<CommentDto> Comments { get; init; }

	/// <summary>Sort order the page was rendered with.</summary>
	public required CommentSortOrder Sort { get; init; }

	/// <summary>Comment from <c>?comment={id}</c>, highlighted and scrolled to.</summary>
	public Guid? HighlightCommentId { get; init; }

	/// <summary>
	/// Supabase origin the browser talks to. Comes straight from
	/// SupabaseOptions.BaseUrl — the local stack in Development,
	/// https://{project-ref}.supabase.co in production. Never composed here.
	/// </summary>
	public required string SupabaseUrl { get; init; }

	/// <summary>Publishable key — public by design, never the secret key.</summary>
	public required string SupabasePublishableKey { get; init; }

	/// <summary>Turnstile site key; empty disables the widget.</summary>
	public required string TurnstileSiteKey { get; init; }

	public int PageSize => Comments.PageSize;

	public int PageNumber => Comments.PageNumber;

	public int TotalCount => Comments.TotalCount;

	public bool HasMore => PageNumber * PageSize < TotalCount;

	/// <summary>Lowercase token used in markup and in the sort links.</summary>
	public string SortValue => Sort == CommentSortOrder.New ? "new" : "top";

	/// <summary>
	/// Rendered into a &lt;script type="application/json"&gt; block. The default
	/// System.Text.Json encoder escapes &lt;, &gt; and &amp;, so the payload can
	/// never terminate the script element early.
	/// </summary>
	public string SupabaseConfigJson => JsonSerializer.Serialize(new Dictionary<string, string>
	{
		["url"] = SupabaseUrl,
		["publishableKey"] = SupabasePublishableKey,
	});
}
```

```csharp
using MediatR;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.RazorPages;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Options;
using MZikmund.DataContracts;
using MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog;
using MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments;
using MZikmund.Web.Configuration;
using MZikmund.Web.Core.Features.Comments;
using MZikmund.Web.Core.Features.Posts;
using MZikmund.Web.Core.Services;

namespace MZikmund.Web.Pages.Blog;

public class PostModel : PageModel, IPostPageModel
{
	private readonly IHostEnvironment _host;
	private readonly IMediator _mediator;
	private readonly IPostContentProcessor _postContentProcessor;
	private readonly CommentsOptions _commentsOptions;
	private readonly SupabaseOptions _supabaseOptions;
	private readonly TurnstileOptions _turnstileOptions;

	public PostModel(
		IHostEnvironment host,
		IMediator mediator,
		IPostContentProcessor postContentProcessor,
		IOptions<CommentsOptions> commentsOptions,
		IOptions<SupabaseOptions> supabaseOptions,
		IOptions<TurnstileOptions> turnstileOptions)
	{
		_host = host;
		_mediator = mediator;
		_postContentProcessor = postContentProcessor;
		_commentsOptions = commentsOptions.Value;
		_supabaseOptions = supabaseOptions.Value;
		_turnstileOptions = turnstileOptions.Value;
	}

	public Post BlogPost { get; set; } = null!;

	public string HtmlContent { get; set; } = "";

	public string MetaKeywords { get; set; } = "";

	public string? SafeHeroImageUrl { get; set; }

	/// <summary>Null when Comments:Enabled is false — the section is not rendered at all.</summary>
	public CommentsSectionModel? CommentsSection { get; set; }

	public async Task OnGet(string routeName, Guid? comment, string? sort)
	{
		BlogPost = await _mediator.Send(new GetPostByRouteNameQuery(routeName));
		HtmlContent = await _postContentProcessor.ProcessAsync(BlogPost.Content);
		MetaKeywords = string.Join(", ", BlogPost.Tags.Select(t => t.DisplayName));

		// Validate and sanitize hero image URL
		// Only allow http:// and https:// URLs for security
		if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(BlogPost.HeroImageUrl) &&
			Uri.TryCreate(BlogPost.HeroImageUrl, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri) &&
			(uri.Scheme == Uri.UriSchemeHttp || uri.Scheme == Uri.UriSchemeHttps))
		{
			SafeHeroImageUrl = uri.ToString();
		}

		if (_commentsOptions.Enabled)
		{
			CommentsSection = await LoadCommentsAsync(comment, sort);
		}
	}

	private async Task<CommentsSectionModel> LoadCommentsAsync(Guid? highlightCommentId, string? sort)
	{
		CommentSortOrder sortOrder = string.Equals(sort, "new", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
			? CommentSortOrder.New
			: CommentSortOrder.Top;

		// A #fragment never reaches the server, so ?comment={id} is what makes a
		// deep-linked comment on page 3 present in the first paint.
		int pageNumber = 1;
		if (highlightCommentId is { } commentId)
		{
			pageNumber = await _mediator.Send(
				new FindCommentPageQuery(commentId, sortOrder, CommentPaging.DefaultPageSize)) ?? 1;
		}

		PagedResponse<CommentDto> comments = await _mediator.Send(
			new GetPostCommentsQuery(BlogPost.Id, sortOrder, pageNumber, CommentPaging.DefaultPageSize));

		return new CommentsSectionModel
		{
			PostId = BlogPost.Id,
			Comments = comments,
			Sort = sortOrder,
			HighlightCommentId = highlightCommentId,
			// BaseUrl, not a composed host: it resolves to Supabase:LocalUrl when one
			// is configured, so Development points the browser at `supabase start`
			// instead of at the production project.
			SupabaseUrl = _supabaseOptions.BaseUrl,
			SupabasePublishableKey = _supabaseOptions.PublishableKey,
			TurnstileSiteKey = _turnstileOptions.SiteKey,
		};
	}
}
```

```razor
@model MZikmund.Web.Pages.Blog.CommentsSectionModel
@using MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments

@{
	// A Razor local function, so the reply markup is written exactly once and
	// stays byte-identical to what CommentRenderer.ts produces client-side.
	void RenderComment(CommentDto comment, bool isReply)
	{
		var showAbsoluteDate = (DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - comment.CreatedOn).TotalDays > 30;
		<article class="comment @(isReply ? "comment--reply" : "")"
				 id="comment-@comment.Id"
				 data-comment-id="@comment.Id"
				 data-parent-id="@(comment.ParentId?.ToString() ?? "")">
			<div class="comment__identity">
				@if (comment.AuthorAvatarUrl is { } avatarUrl)
				{
					<img class="comment__avatar" src="@avatarUrl" alt="" width="32" height="32" loading="lazy" />
				}
				else
				{
					<svg class="icon comment__avatar comment__avatar--fallback" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-person-circle"></use></svg>
				}
				<span class="comment__author">@comment.AuthorDisplayName</span>
				<time class="comment__time" datetime="@comment.CreatedOn.ToString("o")">
					@if (showAbsoluteDate)
					{
						@comment.CreatedOn.ToString("MMM d, yyyy")
					}
					else
					{
						@comment.CreatedOn.Humanize()
					}
				</time>
				@if (comment.EditedOn is not null)
				{
					<span class="comment__edited">@Localizer["edited"]</span>
				}
			</div>

			@if (comment.Status == CommentStatus.DeletedByAuthor)
			{
				<div class="comment__body comment__body--deleted">
					<p>@Localizer["This comment was deleted by its author."]</p>
				</div>
			}
			else
			{
				<div class="comment__body">
					@if (comment.MentionedDisplayName is { } mention)
					{
						<span class="comment__mention">&#64;@mention</span>
					}
					@* Sanitized server-side on write by ICommentContentRenderer. *@
					@Html.Raw(comment.ContentHtml)
				</div>
			}

			<div class="comment__actions">
				<button type="button" class="comment__action" data-comment-upvote
						aria-pressed="false"
						aria-label="@Localizer["Upvote this comment"]">
					<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-hand-thumbs-up"></use></svg>
					<span data-upvote-count>@comment.UpvoteCount</span>
				</button>

				@if (!isReply)
				{
					<button type="button" class="comment__action" data-comment-reply>
						<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-reply"></use></svg>
						@Localizer["Reply"]
					</button>
				}

				<button type="button" class="comment__action comment__action--hidden" data-comment-delete hidden>
					<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-trash3"></use></svg>
					@Localizer["Delete"]
				</button>

				<button type="button" class="comment__action comment__action--hidden" data-comment-report hidden>
					<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-flag"></use></svg>
					@Localizer["Report"]
				</button>
			</div>

			@if (!isReply)
			{
				<div class="comment__replies" data-comment-replies>
					@foreach (var reply in comment.Replies)
					{
						RenderComment(reply, true);
					}
					@if (comment.ReplyCount > comment.Replies.Length)
					{
						<button type="button" class="btn btn--subtle btn--sm comment__more-replies"
								data-load-replies data-reply-page="1">
							@Localizer["Show more replies"] (@(comment.ReplyCount - comment.Replies.Length))
						</button>
					}
				</div>
			}
		</article>
	}
}

<section class="comments" id="comments" aria-labelledby="comments-heading"

		</div>

			<label class="signin-dialog__label" for="signin-code">@Localizer["6-digit code"]</label>
			<input class="signin-dialog__input signin-dialog__input--code" id="signin-code" type="text"
				   inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code" maxlength="6" data-signin-code />
			<button type="button" class="btn btn--accent btn--lg" data-signin-verify>@Localizer["Verify and post"]</button>
		</div>

		<p class="signin-dialog__error" role="alert" data-signin-error></p>
	</dialog>

	@* --- Report ----------------------------------------------------------- *@
	<dialog class="signin-dialog" data-report-dialog aria-labelledby="report-title">
		<form method="dialog" class="signin-dialog__close-form">
			<button class="signin-dialog__close" value="cancel" data-report-close
					aria-label="@Localizer["Close"]" title="@Localizer["Close"]">
				<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-x-lg"></use></svg>
			</button>
		</form>

		<h2 class="signin-dialog__title" id="report-title">@Localizer["Report this comment"]</h2>

		<label class="signin-dialog__label" for="report-reason">@Localizer["Reason"]</label>
		<select class="signin-dialog__input" id="report-reason" data-report-reason>
			<option value="@nameof(CommentReportReason.Spam)">@Localizer["Spam"]</option>
			<option value="@nameof(CommentReportReason.Abuse)">@Localizer["Abuse"]</option>
			<option value="@nameof(CommentReportReason.OffTopic)">@Localizer["Off topic"]</option>
			<option value="@nameof(CommentReportReason.Other)">@Localizer["Other"]</option>
		</select>

		<label class="signin-dialog__label" for="report-note">@Localizer["Note (optional)"]</label>
		<textarea class="signin-dialog__input" id="report-note" rows="3" maxlength="500" data-report-note></textarea>

		<button type="button" class="btn btn--accent btn--lg" data-report-send>@Localizer["Send report"]</button>
		<p class="signin-dialog__error" role="alert" data-report-error></p>
	</dialog>
</section>
```

```razor
@page "/Blog/{RouteName}"
@using System.Linq
@model MZikmund.Web.Pages.Blog.PostModel

@{
	MetaTags.Title = Model.BlogPost?.Title ?? "";
	MetaTags.Description = Model.BlogPost?.Abstract ?? "";
	MetaTags.Keywords = Model.MetaKeywords;
	if (Model.BlogPost?.HeroImageUrl is { } url)
	{
		MetaTags.Image = url;
	}
	if (Model.BlogPost?.HeroImageAlt is { } alt)
	{
		MetaTags.ImageAlt = alt;
	}
}

@section AboveMain
{
    @await Html.PartialAsync("_PostHero", Model)
}

@* .site-main has no top padding and the hero renders above it, so the article
   needs its own gap below the hero divider. *@
<div class="article-layout mt-6">
    <div class="article-layout__main">
        @await Html.PartialAsync("_PostContent", Model)

        @* Deliberately NOT inside _PostContent: that partial is shared with
           PostPreview.cshtml, the unauthenticated share link for unpublished
           drafts, which must never show or accept comments. *@
        @if (Model.CommentsSection is { } commentsSection)
        {
            @await Html.PartialAsync("_Comments", commentsSection)
        }
    </div>

    <aside id="toc-container" class="toc article-layout__aside">
        <!-- Table of Contents will be generated here by JavaScript -->
    </aside>
</div>

<button class="back-to-top" id="back-to-top" type="button" aria-label="Back to top" title="Back to top">
    <svg class="icon icon--lg" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-arrow-up"></use></svg>
</button>

@section BodyEnd
{
    @if (Model.CommentsSection is { } scriptsModel)
    {
        @* Data, not script: a type="application/json" block is never executed,
           and the default STJ encoder escapes < > & so it cannot be closed early. *@
        <script id="supabase-config" type="application/json">@Html.Raw(scriptsModel.SupabaseConfigJson)</script>

        @if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(scriptsModel.TurnstileSiteKey))
        {
            @* Explicit rendering: comments.js owns the widget lifecycle so it can
               reset the single-use token after every submit. *@
            <script src="https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js?render=explicit&onload=mzTurnstileReady" async defer></script>
        }

        <script type="module" src="~/js/comments.js" asp-append-version="true"></script>
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Create the component partial**

Create `src/web/MZikmund.Web/Styles/components/_comments.scss`:

```scss
// =============================================================================
// Comments — a Fluent list of layered cards, a TextBox composer, and the site's
// first true modal surface (the sign-in dialog).
//
// .comment deliberately does NOT reuse .card: _motion.scss gives .card a Reveal
// highlight and a hover lift, and .card__link::after { inset: 0 } assumes one
// stretched link. A comment carries several buttons, so it needs its own block.
// =============================================================================

@layer components {

	.comments {
		margin-block-start: var(--mz-space-9);
		padding-block-start: var(--mz-space-6);
		border-block-start: 1px solid var(--mz-stroke-divider);
		scroll-margin-block-start: calc(var(--mz-header-height) + var(--mz-space-4));
	}

	.comments__header {
		display: flex;
		flex-wrap: wrap;
		align-items: center;
		justify-content: space-between;
		gap: var(--mz-space-3);
		margin-block-end: var(--mz-space-5);
	}

	.comments__title {
		display: flex;
		align-items: center;
		gap: var(--mz-space-2);
		margin: 0;
		font-size: var(--mz-text-title);
		font-weight: var(--mz-weight-semibold);
		line-height: var(--mz-leading-tight);
	}

	.comments__count {
		color: var(--mz-text-tertiary);
		font-weight: var(--mz-weight-regular);
	}

	.comments__sort {
		display: flex;
		gap: var(--mz-space-1);
		padding: var(--mz-space-1);
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-control);
		background-color: var(--mz-shimmer);
	}

	.comments__sort-link {
		padding: var(--mz-space-1) var(--mz-space-3);
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-control);
		color: var(--mz-text-secondary);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);
		font-weight: var(--mz-weight-medium);
		text-decoration: none;
		transition:
			background-color var(--mz-duration-fast) var(--mz-ease-standard),
			color var(--mz-duration-fast) var(--mz-ease-standard);

		&:hover {
			color: var(--mz-text-primary);
		}

		&.is-active {
			background-color: var(--mz-card);
			color: var(--mz-text-primary);
			font-weight: var(--mz-weight-semibold);
			box-shadow: var(--mz-elev-1);
		}
	}

	.comments__list {
		display: flex;
		flex-direction: column;
		gap: var(--mz-space-3);
	}

	.comments__more {
		display: flex;
		justify-content: center;
		margin-block-start: var(--mz-space-5);
	}

	// --- A single comment ----------------------------------------------------
	.comment {
		padding: var(--mz-space-4);
		background-color: var(--mz-card);
		border: 1px solid var(--mz-stroke-card);
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-card);
		// The deep-link target must clear the sticky header when scrolled to.
		scroll-margin-block-start: calc(var(--mz-header-height) + var(--mz-space-4));

		// The global focus halo is painted in --mz-bg-base; on this elevated
		// surface it has to be the card colour instead.
		:focus-visible {
			box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--mz-card);
		}
	}

	.comment.is-highlighted {
		border-color: var(--mz-accent-text);
		box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--mz-accent-text);
	}

	.comment.is-busy {
		opacity: 0.6;
		pointer-events: none;
	}

	.comment__identity {
		display: flex;
		flex-wrap: wrap;
		align-items: center;
		gap: var(--mz-space-2);
		margin-block-end: var(--mz-space-2);
	}

	.comment__avatar {
		width: 2rem;
		height: 2rem;
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-pill);
		object-fit: cover;
	}

	.comment__avatar--fallback {
		color: var(--mz-text-tertiary);
	}

	.comment__author {
		font-size: var(--mz-text-body);
		font-weight: var(--mz-weight-semibold);
		color: var(--mz-text-primary);
	}

	.comment__time,
	.comment__edited {
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);
		color: var(--mz-text-tertiary);
	}

	.comment__mention {
		margin-inline-end: var(--mz-space-1);
		color: var(--mz-accent-text);
		font-weight: var(--mz-weight-semibold);
	}

	// Deliberately not .prose: an article's serif 19px/1.7 is far too heavy for
	// a two-line comment. Only the block rules .prose contributes are repeated.
	.comment__body {
		color: var(--mz-text-primary);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-body);
		line-height: var(--mz-leading-normal);
		overflow-wrap: anywhere;

		p {
			margin-block: 0 var(--mz-space-2);

			&:last-child {
				margin-block-end: 0;
			}
		}

		ul,
		ol {
			margin-block: 0 var(--mz-space-2);
			padding-inline-start: var(--mz-space-5);
		}

		blockquote {
			margin: 0 0 var(--mz-space-2);
			padding-inline-start: var(--mz-space-3);
			border-inline-start: 3px solid var(--mz-stroke-divider);
			color: var(--mz-text-secondary);
		}

		code {
			padding: 0.1em 0.3em;
			border-radius: var(--mz-radius-control);
			background-color: var(--mz-shimmer);
			font-family: var(--mz-font-mono);
			font-size: 0.9em;
		}

		pre {
			margin-block: 0 var(--mz-space-2);
			padding: var(--mz-space-3);
			border-radius: var(--mz-radius-control);
			background-color: var(--mz-bg-secondary);
			overflow-x: auto;

			code {
				padding: 0;
				background: none;
			}
		}
	}

	.comment__body--deleted {
		color: var(--mz-text-tertiary);
		font-style: italic;
	}

	.comment__actions {
		display: flex;
		flex-wrap: wrap;
		gap: var(--mz-space-1);
		margin-block-start: var(--mz-space-2);
	}

	.comment__action {
		display: inline-flex;
		align-items: center;
		gap: var(--mz-space-1);
		padding: var(--mz-space-1) var(--mz-space-2);
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-control);
		color: var(--mz-text-secondary);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);
		font-weight: var(--mz-weight-medium);
		transition:
			background-color var(--mz-duration-fast) var(--mz-ease-standard),
			color var(--mz-duration-fast) var(--mz-ease-standard);

		&:hover {
			background-color: var(--mz-shimmer);
			color: var(--mz-text-primary);
		}

		&[aria-pressed="true"] {
			background-color: var(--mz-accent-subtle);
			color: var(--mz-accent-text);
		}
	}

	// --- Replies -------------------------------------------------------------
	// One level only, and the indent has to survive a 68ch column at 360px.
	.comment__replies {
		display: flex;
		flex-direction: column;
		gap: var(--mz-space-3);
		margin-block-start: var(--mz-space-3);
		padding-inline-start: var(--mz-space-4);
		border-inline-start: 2px solid var(--mz-stroke-divider);

		&:empty {
			display: none;
		}
	}

	.comment--reply {
		padding: var(--mz-space-3);
		background-color: var(--mz-bg-tertiary);
	}

	.comment__more-replies {
		align-self: flex-start;
	}

	// --- Composer ------------------------------------------------------------
	// The WinUI TextBox idiom: layered fill, hairline border, and an accent
	// underline that thickens on focus.
	.comment-composer {
		display: flex;
		flex-direction: column;
		gap: var(--mz-space-3);
		margin-block-end: var(--mz-space-6);
		padding: var(--mz-space-4);
		background-color: var(--mz-card);
		border: 1px solid var(--mz-stroke-card);
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-card);
	}

	.comment-composer__reply-to {
		display: flex;
		align-items: center;
		justify-content: space-between;
		gap: var(--mz-space-2);
		padding: var(--mz-space-2) var(--mz-space-3);
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-control);
		background-color: var(--mz-accent-subtle);
		color: var(--mz-accent-text);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);
	}

	.comment-composer__input {
		width: 100%;
		padding: var(--mz-space-3);
		background-color: var(--mz-bg-tertiary);
		border: 1px solid var(--mz-stroke-control);
		border-block-end-width: 2px;
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-control);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-body);
		line-height: var(--mz-leading-normal);
		resize: vertical;
		transition: border-color var(--mz-duration-fast) var(--mz-ease-standard);

		&:hover {
			background-color: var(--mz-bg-secondary);
		}

		&:focus {
			outline: none;
			background-color: var(--mz-bg-elevated);
			border-block-end-color: var(--mz-accent-fill);
		}

		&::placeholder {
			color: var(--mz-text-tertiary);
		}
	}

	.comment-composer__footer {
		display: flex;
		flex-wrap: wrap;
		align-items: center;
		justify-content: flex-end;
		gap: var(--mz-space-3);
	}

	.comment-composer__counter {
		margin: 0;
		margin-inline-end: auto;
		color: var(--mz-text-tertiary);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);
		font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
	}

	.comment-composer__turnstile {
		min-width: 0;

		&:empty {
			display: none;
		}
	}

	.comment-composer__status {
		margin: 0;
		color: var(--mz-text-secondary);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);

		&:empty {
			display: none;
		}
	}

	// --- Modal dialog --------------------------------------------------------
	// The site's first modal. Acrylic like the theme flyout, but WITH a Smoke
	// scrim — Fluent reserves dimming for modal surfaces.
	.signin-dialog {
		width: min(24rem, calc(100vw - var(--mz-space-6)));
		padding: var(--mz-space-6);
		border: 1px solid var(--mz-stroke-card);
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-overlay);
		background-color: var(--mz-acrylic);
		color: var(--mz-text-primary);
		box-shadow: var(--mz-elev-4);

		@supports (backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) {
			-webkit-backdrop-filter: var(--mz-acrylic-blur);
			backdrop-filter: var(--mz-acrylic-blur);
		}

		&::backdrop {
			background-color: var(--mz-smoke);
		}

		&[open] {
			@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
				animation: mz-dialog-in var(--mz-duration-normal) var(--mz-ease-entrance);
			}
		}
	}

	@keyframes mz-dialog-in {
		from {
			opacity: 0;
			scale: 0.96;
		}

		to {
			opacity: 1;
			scale: 1;
		}
	}

	.signin-dialog__close-form {
		display: flex;
		justify-content: flex-end;
	}

	.signin-dialog__close {
		padding: var(--mz-space-1);
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-control);
		color: var(--mz-text-secondary);

		&:hover {
			background-color: var(--mz-shimmer);
			color: var(--mz-text-primary);
		}
	}

	.signin-dialog__title {
		margin: 0 0 var(--mz-space-2);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-subtitle);
		font-weight: var(--mz-weight-semibold);
	}

	.signin-dialog__lead {
		margin: 0 0 var(--mz-space-5);
		color: var(--mz-text-secondary);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);
	}

	.signin-dialog__providers {
		display: flex;
		flex-direction: column;
		gap: var(--mz-space-2);
	}

	.signin-dialog__divider {
		display: flex;
		align-items: center;
		gap: var(--mz-space-3);
		margin-block: var(--mz-space-5);
		color: var(--mz-text-tertiary);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);

		&::before,
		&::after {
			content: "";
			flex: 1;
			height: 1px;
			background-color: var(--mz-stroke-divider);
		}
	}

	.signin-dialog__step {
		display: flex;
		flex-direction: column;
		gap: var(--mz-space-2);
	}

	.signin-dialog__label {
		color: var(--mz-text-secondary);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);
		font-weight: var(--mz-weight-medium);
	}

	.signin-dialog__input {
		width: 100%;
		padding: var(--mz-space-2) var(--mz-space-3);
		background-color: var(--mz-bg-tertiary);
		border: 1px solid var(--mz-stroke-control);
		border-block-end-width: 2px;
		border-radius: var(--mz-radius-control);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-body);

		&:focus {
			outline: none;
			background-color: var(--mz-bg-elevated);
			border-block-end-color: var(--mz-accent-fill);
		}
	}

	.signin-dialog__input--code {
		letter-spacing: 0.4em;
		font-family: var(--mz-font-mono);
		text-align: center;
	}

	.signin-dialog__error {
		margin: var(--mz-space-3) 0 0;
		color: var(--mz-text-primary);
		font-size: var(--mz-text-caption);

		&:empty {
			display: none;
		}
	}
}
```

Create `src/web/MZikmund.Web/Scripts/Auth/SupabaseAuth.ts`:

```ts
import {
	createClient,
	type Session,
	type SupabaseClient,
} from "@supabase/supabase-js";

interface SupabaseAuthConfig {
	url: string;            // https://<project-ref>.supabase.co
	publishableKey: string; // sb_publishable_...  (NEVER the secret key)
}

let client: SupabaseClient | null = null;

/** Reads the JSON block Razor renders into the page. Never inline the key here. */
function readConfig(): SupabaseAuthConfig {
	const el = document.getElementById("supabase-config");
	if (!el?.textContent) {
		throw new Error("Missing #supabase-config JSON block.");
	}
	return JSON.parse(el.textContent) as SupabaseAuthConfig;
}

export function getClient(): SupabaseClient {
	if (client) {
		return client;
	}
	const cfg = readConfig();
	client = createClient(cfg.url, cfg.publishableKey, {
		auth: {
			// The library default is 'implicit', which puts the access token in
			// the URL fragment where it leaks via history and Referer. PKCE must
			// be requested explicitly.
			flowType: "pkce",
			// Consumes ?code= on the OAuth return and strips it with
			// history.replaceState. Default is true; stated for the reader.
			detectSessionInUrl: true,
			persistSession: true,
			autoRefreshToken: true,
			// Pinned so a library change to the default key shape cannot sign
			// everyone out. Documented in design-system.md.
			storage: window.localStorage,
			storageKey: "mz-auth",
		},
	});
	return client;
}

// --- Sign-in ---------------------------------------------------------------
// signInWithOAuth navigates the tab away, so nothing after it runs. returnTo
// must be on the Redirect URLs allow list in the Supabase dashboard.

export function signInWithGoogle(returnTo: string): Promise<unknown> {
	return getClient().auth.signInWithOAuth({
		provider: "google",
		options: { redirectTo: returnTo },
	});
}

export function signInWithApple(returnTo: string): Promise<unknown> {
	return getClient().auth.signInWithOAuth({
		provider: "apple",
		options: { redirectTo: returnTo },
	});
}

/**
 * Sends the 6-digit code. Code vs. magic link is decided by the Supabase email
 * template: `{{ .Token }}` is a code, `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}` is a link.
 */
export async function sendEmailCode(email: string): Promise<void> {
	const { error } = await getClient().auth.signInWithOtp({
		email,
		options: { shouldCreateUser: true },
	});
	if (error) {
		throw error;
	}
}

/** type "email" covers both first sign-up and returning sign-in; "signup" and
 *  "magiclink" are deprecated. */
export async function verifyEmailCode(email: string, token: string): Promise<Session> {
	const { data, error } = await getClient().auth.verifyOtp({ email, token, type: "email" });
	if (error || !data.session) {
		throw error ?? new Error("No session returned.");
	}
	return data.session;
}

// --- Session ---------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Reads from storage. The background ticker keeps the token fresh, so this
 * returns without a network call. It does NOT revalidate the JWT — the API
 * validates it against the Supabase JWKS, which is where the real check lives.
 */
export async function getSession(): Promise<Session | null> {
	const { data } = await getClient().auth.getSession();
	return data.session;
}

export async function getAccessToken(): Promise<string | null> {
	return (await getSession())?.access_token ?? null;
}

/** scope defaults to 'global', which kills the session on every device. */
export async function signOut(): Promise<void> {
	await getClient().auth.signOut({ scope: "local" });
}

// --- Calling this site's own API -------------------------------------------

/**
 * Same-origin call to /api/v1/... with the Supabase access token attached.
 * No CORS involved: the site and the API share one origin.
 */
export async function apiFetch(input: string, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> {
	const token = await getAccessToken();
	const headers = new Headers(init.headers);
	if (token) {
		headers.set("Authorization", `Bearer ${token}`);
	}
	if (init.body && !headers.has("Content-Type")) {
		headers.set("Content-Type", "application/json");
	}
	return fetch(input, { ...init, headers, credentials: "same-origin" });
}
```

Create `src/web/MZikmund.Web/Scripts/Comments/CommentsApi.ts`:

```ts
import { apiFetch } from "../Auth/SupabaseAuth";

/** Mirrors MZikmund.DataContracts.Blog.Comments.CommentDto. Property names are
 *  camelCase (ASP.NET default) and enums are strings (JsonStringEnumConverter). */
export interface CommentDto {
	id: string;
	postId: string;
	parentId: string | null;
	authorDisplayName: string;
	authorAvatarUrl: string | null;
	mentionedDisplayName: string | null;
	content: string;
	contentHtml: string;
	status: "Visible" | "DeletedByAuthor" | "HiddenByModerator";
	createdOn: string;
	editedOn: string | null;
	upvoteCount: number;
	replyCount: number;
	hasUpvoted: boolean;
	isOwn: boolean;
	replies: CommentDto[];
}

export interface PagedResponse<T> {
	data: T[];
	pageNumber: number;
	pageSize: number;
	totalCount: number;
}

export type CommentSort = "top" | "new";

export type ReportReason = "Spam" | "Abuse" | "OffTopic" | "Other";

export class ApiError extends Error {
	public readonly status: number;
	public readonly retryAfterSeconds: number | null;

	public constructor(status: number, retryAfterSeconds: number | null, message: string) {
		super(message);
		this.name = "ApiError";
		this.status = status;
		this.retryAfterSeconds = retryAfterSeconds;
	}
}

function toApiError(response: Response): ApiError {
	const header = response.headers.get("Retry-After");
	const retryAfter = header === null ? null : Number.parseInt(header, 10);
	return new ApiError(
		response.status,
		Number.isFinite(retryAfter) ? retryAfter : null,
		`Request failed with status ${response.status}.`
	);
}

async function readJson<T>(response: Response): Promise<T> {
	if (!response.ok) {
		throw toApiError(response);
	}
	return (await response.json()) as T;
}

export function getComments(
	postId: string,
	sort: CommentSort,
	pageNumber: number,
	pageSize: number
): Promise<PagedResponse<CommentDto>> {
	const url = `/api/v1/posts/${postId}/comments?sort=${sort}&pageNumber=${pageNumber}&pageSize=${pageSize}`;
	return apiFetch(url).then((r) => readJson<PagedResponse<CommentDto>>(r));
}

export function getReplies(
	commentId: string,
	pageNumber: number,
	pageSize: number
): Promise<PagedResponse<CommentDto>> {
	const url = `/api/v1/comments/${commentId}/replies?pageNumber=${pageNumber}&pageSize=${pageSize}`;
	return apiFetch(url).then((r) => readJson<PagedResponse<CommentDto>>(r));
}

/**
 * The Turnstile token travels in the CF-Turnstile-Response header, never in the
 * body — the DTO is shared with the native app, which has no captcha. The server
 * contract is: if the header is present it must verify; absence is permitted.
 */
export async function createComment(
	postId: string,
	content: string,
	parentId: string | null,
	turnstileToken: string | null
): Promise<CommentDto> {
	const headers: Record<string, string> = {};
	if (turnstileToken) {
		headers["CF-Turnstile-Response"] = turnstileToken;
	}

	const response = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/posts/${postId}/comments`, {
		method: "POST",
		headers,
		body: JSON.stringify({ content, parentId }),
	});

	return readJson<CommentDto>(response);
}

export async function deleteComment(commentId: string): Promise<void> {
	const response = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/comments/${commentId}`, { method: "DELETE" });
	if (!response.ok) {
		throw toApiError(response);
	}
}

export async function setVote(commentId: string, upvoted: boolean): Promise<CommentDto> {
	const response = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/comments/${commentId}/vote`, {
		method: upvoted ? "PUT" : "DELETE",
	});
	return readJson<CommentDto>(response);
}

export async function reportComment(
	commentId: string,
	reason: ReportReason,
	note: string | null
): Promise<void> {
	const response = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/comments/${commentId}/report`, {
		method: "POST",
		body: JSON.stringify({ reason, note }),
	});
	if (!response.ok) {
		throw toApiError(response);
	}
}
```

```ts
// Ambient declarations for the Cloudflare Turnstile api.js global. A .d.ts
// emits nothing into the bundle, so this costs zero bytes and avoids an
// @types devDependency.

interface TurnstileRenderOptions {
	sitekey: string;
	action?: string;
	cData?: string;
	callback?: (token: string) => void;
	"error-callback"?: (errorCode: string) => void;
	"expired-callback"?: () => void;
	"timeout-callback"?: () => void;
	theme?: "light" | "dark" | "auto";
	language?: string;
	size?: "normal" | "flexible" | "compact";

	retry?: "auto" | "never";
	"retry-interval"?: number;
	"refresh-expired"?: "auto" | "manual" | "never";
	"refresh-timeout"?: "auto" | "manual" | "never";
	appearance?: "always" | "execute" | "interaction-only";

}
```

Create `src/web/MZikmund.Web/Scripts/Comments/CommentTurnstile.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Owns the single Turnstile widget in the comment composer.
 *
 * A token is single-use and lives 300 seconds, so it is reset after EVERY
 * submit, not only after a failure — otherwise the reader's second comment in
 * one page session replays a spent token and siteverify returns
 * `timeout-or-duplicate`, which looks like a captcha failure but is a client bug.
 */
export class CommentTurnstile {
	private widgetId: string | undefined;
	private token: string | null = null;
	private waiters: ((token: string | null) => void)[] = [];

	public render(container: HTMLElement, siteKey: string): void {
		if (!siteKey) {
			return;
		}

		const draw = (): void => {
			this.widgetId = turnstile.render(container, {
				sitekey: siteKey,
				action: "comment-create",
				theme: this.currentTheme(),
				size: "flexible",
				"refresh-expired": "auto",
				// No hidden input: the token rides in the CF-Turnstile-Response
				// header, and the composer never does a plain form post.
				"response-field": false,
				callback: (token: string) => this.settle(token),
				"error-callback": () => this.settle(null),
				"expired-callback": () => {
					this.token = null;
				},
				"timeout-callback": () => this.settle(null),
			});
		};

		// api.js is async+defer, so it may load before or after this module. If
		// the global is already there, render now; otherwise let ?onload= call us.
		if (typeof turnstile !== "undefined") {
			turnstile.ready(draw);
		} else {
			window.mzTurnstileReady = () => turnstile.ready(draw);
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Resolves with the current token, waiting for the challenge to solve itself
	 * if it has not yet. Resolves with null on timeout or error — the server
	 * permits an absent token (that is what keeps the native app able to post),
	 * so a stuck widget must never block the reader.
	 */
	public getToken(timeoutMs = 8000): Promise<string | null> {
		if (this.widgetId === undefined) {
			return Promise.resolve(null);
		}

		if (this.token && !turnstile.isExpired(this.widgetId)) {
			return Promise.resolve(this.token);
		}

		const existing = turnstile.getResponse(this.widgetId);
		if (existing) {
			this.token = existing;
			return Promise.resolve(existing);
		}

		return new Promise<string | null>((resolve) => {
			const timer = window.setTimeout(() => {
				this.waiters = this.waiters.filter((w) => w !== waiter);
				resolve(null);
			}, timeoutMs);

			const waiter = (token: string | null): void => {
				window.clearTimeout(timer);
				resolve(token);
			};

			this.waiters.push(waiter);
		});
	}

	public reset(): void {
		this.token = null;
		if (this.widgetId !== undefined) {
			turnstile.reset(this.widgetId);
		}
	}

	private settle(token: string | null): void {
		this.token = token;
		const waiters = this.waiters;
		this.waiters = [];
		for (const waiter of waiters) {
			waiter(token);
		}
	}

	// ThemeSwitchManager guarantees data-theme is a concrete value, never "auto".
	private currentTheme(): "light" | "dark" {
		return document.documentElement.getAttribute("data-theme") === "dark" ? "dark" : "light";
	}
}
```
