```cshtml
@page
@model PrivacyModel
@{
    MetaTags.Title = "Privacy Policy";
}

<div class="prose-page prose">
    <h1>Privacy Policy</h1>
    <p>Effective Date: August 11, 2026</p>

    <p>Your privacy is important to us. This Privacy Policy explains what information mzikmund.dev
        ("the Site") and the companion Martin Zikmund app ("the App") collect, why, and what you can do
        about it. The Site is operated by Martin Zikmund, who is the data controller for the processing
        described here.</p>

    <h2>1. Reading the Site</h2>
    <p>You can read every article, video listing and page on the Site without an account and without
        telling us who you are. Reading is anonymous.</p>
    <p>When you visit, our hosting platform and our diagnostics service record technical request data —
        including your IP address, browser user agent, the pages you requested and the time of the
        request — so we can keep the Site running and diagnose faults. Your colour theme preference
        (auto, light or dark) is stored in your own browser and is never sent to us.</p>

    <h2>2. Advertising</h2>
    <p>The Site displays advertising from Google AdSense. Google and its partners may set cookies and
        similar identifiers in your browser to serve and measure ads. We do not receive your identity
        from Google. Where the law requires your consent for those cookies, the consent message is
        presented by Google itself rather than by us; the Site sets no consent cookie of its own. You
        can review and change your ad settings at
        <a href="https://myadcenter.google.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Google My Ad Center</a>
        and read
        <a href="https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites" target="_blank" rel="noopener">how Google uses information from sites that use its services</a>.</p>

    <h2>3. Signing In</h2>
    <p>You only need an account to post a comment, reply, upvote or report a comment. Sign-in is handled
        for us by <a href="https://supabase.com/privacy" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Supabase</a>,
        which acts as our processor and holds your account record: a user identifier, your email
        address, which sign-in method you used, and sign-in timestamps. We never see or store a
        password — password sign-in is disabled.</p>
    <p>You can sign in in three ways, and each shares a different amount of information with us:</p>
    <ul>
        <li><strong>Google.</strong> We request the standard <code>openid</code>, email and profile
            scopes. Google returns your email address, your name and the web address of your Google
            profile picture.</li>
        <li><strong>Apple.</strong> Apple returns your email address, or a private relay address ending
            in <code>@@privaterelay.appleid.com</code> if you chose to hide your email. Apple does not
            provide a profile picture, and provides your name only at the moment you first authorise
            the Site.</li>
        <li><strong>Email code.</strong> You enter an email address and we send a six-digit code to it.
            We receive nothing beyond that address.</li>
    </ul>

    <h2>4. Information We Store About Commenters</h2>
    <p>When you post, edit, upvote or report a comment, we create or update a record about you in our
        own database. It is built from your sign-in token — never from anything the browser or the App
        submits — and it contains:</p>
    <ul>
        <li>Your Supabase user identifier.</li>
        <li>Your display name, as shown next to your comments.</li>
        <li>The web address of your profile picture, where your sign-in provider supplied one. The
            image itself stays on your provider's servers; your browser loads it from there when a page
            shows it.</li>
        <li>Your email address (see section 6).</li>
        <li>Whether you are currently blocked from posting (see section 9).</li>
        <li>Your reply-notification preference, and the dates you first signed in and were last seen.</li>
    </ul>

    <h2>5. Comments, Votes and Reports</h2>
    <p>The text of your comment is stored exactly as you wrote it, together with a rendered copy used to
        display it, the time you posted it and the time of any edit. <strong>Comments are public.</strong>
        Your comment, your display name and your profile picture are visible to every visitor, are
        included in the page's HTML, and can therefore be indexed by search engines and copied by
        others. Please do not put anything private in a comment.</p>
    <p>Upvotes are stored as a link between your account and the comment you voted on, so that a vote
        counts once and can be undone. Only the total is shown publicly; who voted is not.</p>
    <p>If you report a comment, we store which comment you reported, the reason you selected, any note
        you added, and the fact that the report came from you. Reports are visible to the moderator,
        not to the public and not to the author of the reported comment.</p>

    <h2>6. Your Email Address and Future Notifications</h2>
    <p>Your email address is stored with your commenter record. It is <strong>never displayed
        publicly</strong> and never shared with other users. We do not currently send any email from the
        Site — reply notifications are not switched on. We retain your address so that reply
        notifications can be enabled later without asking you to sign in again, and your notification
        preference is stored alongside it. If and when notifications are enabled, you will be able to
        turn them off, and this policy will be updated before any message is sent.</p>

    <h2>7. Preventing Spam and Abuse</h2>
    <p>To stop automated and abusive posting we apply rate limits to the comment endpoints. These are
        counted against your account when you are signed in, and against your IP address otherwise. IP
        addresses are used transiently for this purpose and are not stored alongside your comments.</p>
    <p>The comment form on the Site is protected by
        <a href="https://www.cloudflare.com/turnstile-privacy-policy/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Cloudflare Turnstile</a>,
        which acts as our processor. Turnstile loads a widget from <code>challenges.cloudflare.com</code>
        and processes your IP address, TLS fingerprint, user-agent header and our site key in order to
        distinguish people from bots. It may set Cloudflare cookies in your browser as part of that
        check. We receive only a pass or fail result, which we verify with Cloudflare on our server
        before accepting your comment.</p>

    <h2>8. Cookies and Browser Storage</h2>
    <p>The Site itself does not set tracking cookies and does not use a consent banner. The following
        items are stored in your own browser:</p>
    <ul>
        <li><strong>Your sign-in session.</strong> After you sign in, the Supabase client library keeps
            your session in your browser's local storage under the key <code>mz-auth</code>, plus a
            short-lived <code>mz-auth-code-verifier</code> entry used while the sign-in redirect
            completes. This is what keeps you signed in; signing out or clearing site data removes
            it.</li>
        <li><strong>Your comment draft.</strong> If you start writing before signing in, your draft is
            saved in session storage so it survives the trip to your sign-in provider and back. It is
            discarded when the comment is posted or the tab is closed.</li>
        <li><strong>Your theme preference.</strong> Stored locally so the Site does not flash the wrong
            colours.</li>
        <li><strong>Advertising and bot-protection cookies</strong> set by Google and Cloudflare as
            described in sections 2 and 7.</li>
    </ul>
    <p>The first three are necessary to provide features you asked for and are not used to track you.</p>

    <h2>9. Data Retention and Deletion</h2>
    <p>Comments are kept for as long as the article they belong to is published.</p>
    <p>When you delete your own comment it stops being shown and is replaced by a placeholder, so that
        any replies underneath it are not orphaned. The underlying record — including the fact that you
        wrote it, and when — is retained. The same is true when a moderator hides a comment.</p>
    <p>If a comment breaks the rules we may block an account from posting further comments. That block
        is retained for as long as it is in force. Existing comments from a blocked account are not
        automatically removed, and are hidden individually where warranted.</p>
    <p>If you ask us to erase your data, we will remove the content of your comments, your display name,
        your profile picture address and your email address, and delete your sign-in account. Where a
        comment has replies we keep an anonymous placeholder in its place, so the conversation stays
        readable.</p>

    <h2>10. Your Rights</h2>
    <p>You can ask us at any time for a copy of the information we hold about you, or to correct it,
        erase it, restrict how we use it, or object to our use of it. You can also ask us to hand your
        data to you in a portable form. You can edit your own comment for a short window after posting,
        and delete it at any time, without contacting us.</p>
    <p>We process comment data in order to provide the commenting feature you asked to use, and we
        process spam-prevention and moderation data on the basis of our legitimate interest in keeping
        the discussion usable.</p>
    <p>Write to us using the address in section 15 and we will respond within one month. If you believe
        we have handled your data badly, you may complain to your local data protection authority; in
        the Czech Republic this is the Office for Personal Data Protection
        (<a href="https://www.uoou.gov.cz/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">uoou.gov.cz</a>).</p>

    <h2>11. Who Else Sees Your Data</h2>
    <p>We do not sell your data and do not share it beyond the service providers we need in order to run
        the Site:</p>
    <ul>
        <li><strong>Supabase</strong> — sign-in and account storage.</li>
        <li><strong>Google</strong> and <strong>Apple</strong> — only if you choose to sign in with them.</li>
        <li><strong>Cloudflare</strong> — bot protection on the comment form.</li>
        <li><strong>Microsoft Azure</strong> — hosting, database and diagnostics.</li>
        <li><strong>Google AdSense</strong> — advertising.</li>
    </ul>
    <p>Some of these providers are based outside the European Economic Area, and data may therefore be
        transferred internationally under the safeguards those providers offer, such as standard
        contractual clauses.</p>

    <h2>12. Children</h2>
    <p>The Site is not directed at children under the age of 13, and we do not knowingly collect
        personal information from them. You must be at least 16 years of age to consent to the
        processing of your personal information in your country (in some countries a parent or guardian
        may do so on your behalf). If you believe a child has provided personal information through the
        Site, please contact us so that we can remove it.</p>

    <h2>13. Data Security</h2>
    <p>We take reasonable measures to protect your data from unauthorized access or disclosure:
        everything is served over HTTPS, comment content is sanitized on our server before it is ever
        displayed, and access to the database is restricted. However, please be aware that no method of
        transmission over the Internet or method of electronic storage is 100% secure.</p>

    <h2>14. Changes to This Privacy Policy</h2>
    <p>We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Any changes will be posted on this page with
        an updated effective date. You are advised to consult this Privacy Policy regularly, as
        continued use of the Site is deemed approval of all changes.</p>

    <h2>15. Contact Us</h2>
    <p>If you have any questions or concerns about this Privacy Policy, or want to exercise any of the
        rights in section 10, please contact us at:</p>
    <p>Email: martin@zikmund.dev</p>

    <p>Thank you for reading, and for commenting.</p>
</div>
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the runbook**

Write this as the complete contents of `docs/COMMENTS_ROLLOUT.md`:

````markdown
# Comments Rollout Runbook

Dark-launch procedure for the comments feature. Deploy dark, smoke-test in production against the
ungated admin routes, then switch on. Every step is reversible.

- **App Service:** `webapp-mzikmund`, resource group `mzikmund`
- **Feature gate:** `Comments:Enabled` → `CommentsOptions` in `MZikmund.Web.Configuration`
- **App Service setting name:** `Comments__Enabled` (double underscore is the nesting separator)

## Why the admin routes are not gated

The `Comments:Enabled` action filter returns **404** on the public comment routes only. The routes
under `api/v1/admin/comments` are deliberately left ungated so that moderation can be exercised in
production while the feature is invisible to readers. This is a design decision, not an oversight.

The Uno app has no visibility of the flag and shows an empty comments section while dark.

## 0. Preconditions

Supabase auth must already be live in production — the policy and the smoke test both describe
Supabase, not Auth0. Verify the committed configuration:

```bash
grep -n "Supabase\|Auth0" src/web/MZikmund.Web/appsettings.json
```

Expect a `Supabase` section with `ProjectRef` and `PublishableKey`, and **no** `Auth0` section. If
`Auth0` is still there, stop: the auth phase has not landed and none of this applies yet.

Record the two values for later:

```bash
grep -A3 '"Supabase"' src/web/MZikmund.Web/appsettings.json
```

## 1. Confirm the committed default is OFF

```bash
grep -A2 '"Comments"' src/web/MZikmund.Web/appsettings.json
```

Expected:

```json
	"Comments": {
		"Enabled": false
	},
```

A committed `true` here means a deploy would switch the feature on for everyone the moment it lands.
Fix that before deploying.

## 2. Pin the flag OFF in App Service *before* the deploy

The App Service setting overrides the committed value, so set it first. This makes the flag
independent of what any future deploy happens to carry.

```bash
az webapp config appsettings set \
  --name webapp-mzikmund \
  --resource-group mzikmund \
  --settings Comments__Enabled=false
```

Confirm:

```bash
az webapp config appsettings list \
  --name webapp-mzikmund \
  --resource-group mzikmund \
  --query "[?name=='Comments__Enabled'].value" -o tsv
```

Expected output: `false`

Also confirm the Turnstile secret is present (it is an App Service setting, never committed):

```bash
az webapp config appsettings list \
  --name webapp-mzikmund \
  --resource-group mzikmund \
  --query "[?name=='Turnstile__SecretKey'].name" -o tsv
```

Expected output: `Turnstile__SecretKey`

## 3. Deploy

Merge to `main`. `.github/workflows/azure-publish.yml` builds and deploys automatically. Watch it:

```bash
gh run watch
```

Wait for `Build and deploy Azure Web App` to complete successfully. The database migration runs on
startup (`Program.cs` auto-migrates), so the comment tables are created by this deploy even though
the feature is dark.

## 4. Mint an admin access token

Password sign-in is disabled, so use the email-OTP path against GoTrue directly. Substitute the
project ref and publishable key recorded in step 0.

Request the code:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/otp" \
  -H "apikey: <publishable-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"martin@zikmund.dev","create_user":false}'
```

Expected response body: `{}`

Read the six-digit code from the inbox, then exchange it:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/verify" \
  -H "apikey: <publishable-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"type":"email","email":"martin@zikmund.dev","token":"<six-digit-code>"}'
```

Copy the `access_token` from the response:

```bash
export TOKEN="<access_token>"
```

Sanity-check that the token actually carries the admin role — the role lives in `app_metadata.role`,
never in the user-editable `user_metadata`:

```bash
echo "$TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"role":"[^"]*"'
```

Expected output includes: `"role":"admin"`

## 5. Dark smoke test

**Public routes must be dark.** Pick any published post id from the blog and:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  "https://mzikmund.dev/api/v1/posts/<post-id>/comments?pageNumber=1"
```

Expected output: `404`

The post page itself must render normally with no comments section:

```bash
curl -s "https://mzikmund.dev/blog/<route-name>" | grep -c "comments__composer"
```

Expected output: `0`

**Admin routes must work.** These are deliberately not gated.

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://mzikmund.dev/api/v1/admin/comments?pageNumber=1"
```

Expected output: `200`

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://mzikmund.dev/api/v1/admin/comments/reports?pageNumber=1"
```

Expected output: `200`

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://mzikmund.dev/api/v1/admin/comments/count"
```

Expected output: `0` — the table is empty and the query, the connection and the migration all work.

**Admin routes must reject non-admins.** Without a token:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  "https://mzikmund.dev/api/v1/admin/comments?pageNumber=1"
```

Expected output: `401`

**The privacy policy must be live and linked**, because it goes public with the deploy, before the
feature does:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "https://mzikmund.dev/privacy"
curl -s "https://mzikmund.dev/" | grep -c 'href="/privacy"'
```

Expected output:

```
200
1
```

If any expectation above fails, **do not switch on**. Go to section 8.

## 6. Switch on

```bash
az webapp config appsettings set \
  --name webapp-mzikmund \
  --resource-group mzikmund \
  --settings Comments__Enabled=true
```

Setting an app setting restarts the site. Wait for it to come back:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "https://mzikmund.dev/"
```

Expected output: `200`

## 7. Post-switch verification

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  "https://mzikmund.dev/api/v1/posts/<post-id>/comments?pageNumber=1"
```

Expected output: `200`

```bash
curl -s "https://mzikmund.dev/blog/<route-name>" | grep -c "comments__composer"
```

Expected output: `1`

Then, in a real browser on a real post page:

1. The composer is visible and enabled while signed out.
2. Type a comment, press Post → the sign-in dialog appears and the draft survives the round trip.
3. Sign in with Google → the comment posts and appears immediately.
4. Upvote it, reload → the vote persists and the count is 1.
5. Delete it → it renders as a tombstone placeholder, not a gap.
6. The "By posting you agree to the privacy policy." link under the composer resolves to `/privacy`.

Then in the Uno app, sign in as a **non-admin** reader and confirm the Admin navigation section is
**not** shown — `WindowShellViewModel.IsAdmin` gates it, not `IsLoggedIn`.

## 8. Rollback

One command, no deploy, no revert:

```bash
az webapp config appsettings set \
  --name webapp-mzikmund \
  --resource-group mzikmund \
  --settings Comments__Enabled=false
```

Confirm the public routes are dark again:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  "https://mzikmund.dev/api/v1/posts/<post-id>/comments?pageNumber=1"
```

Expected output: `404`

Comments already posted are retained in the database and reappear when the flag is set back to
`true`. Rolling back does **not** delete data.

If the problem is worse than the feature — a broken asset pipeline, a failing migration — redeploy
the previous successful run instead:

```bash
gh run list --workflow=azure-publish.yml --limit 5
gh run rerun <run-id>
```
````
